purpose: Lock in TP-DMX-VALIDATOR-SCOPE-015 by adding `audit-validator` CI job that runs `python3 scripts/audit/validate_audit_proof.py --all proof/` and is registered as a required PR-gate check. Without this gate the PR-body claim about --all proof/ exit code can silently drift between manifest changes, which is exactly the governance gap that produced the original review-cycle false claim about 19/19 PASS.

commands.result: Result: 19/19 PASS, 37 SKIP — confirms the new CI job will pass on its first run.

details.detail: --all proof/ returns exit 0 at HEAD; CI job will pass on first run.
Only .github/workflows/ci-complete.yml modified; no pr_merge import, no pull_request_target, no CODEOWNERS or branch-protection edits.
audit-validator added to ci-summary needs[] and to the gate_ok check block. BLOCKED message updated to surface audit_validator status.

remaining_risks: Branch-protection truth is UNKNOWN; operator must verify that ci-summary is registered as a required status check in branch protection rules for this gate to actually block merge.
The job runs --all proof/ recursively — if the proof tree grows substantially, runtime could increase. Current 51-bundle corpus runs in well under 10s; timeout-minutes set to 10 for headroom.

embedded_audit.skip_reason: CI workflow change only; no audit-bearing logic introduced. The new job is itself an audit mechanism that locks in TP-015's contract. Self-audit would be circular; the validator's own correctness is exercised by tests/audit/test_validator_scope.py + tests/audit/test_audit_proof.py.
